title: A text layer's box is its words
goal: Select a piece of text and the box drawn round it sits a few points wider and taller than the words, because a measured text box carries empty room on its far edges so the letters never clip. Make what you select, what you measure and what the W and H fields say all be the words.
notes: TextMeasurement.slack (4pt, = TextRasterizer.frameInset * 2) sits inside Layer.frame on the far edges. Layer.contentBounds already names the visible box and GroupFlow now flows by it (2026-09-04). Everything else - selection rendering, LayerGeometryEditing, Measure, snapping - still reads localBounds. Options: keep the slack in the frame and make the UI read contentBounds everywhere, or take the slack out of the frame entirely and have DocumentRenderer/TextRasterizer outset when rasterizing (bigger: needs a document migration or every saved text box re-wraps).
acceptance: Selecting a label draws its box flush to the words on all four sides
The W and H fields for a label report the size of the words, and typing into them still wraps the words to that width
Measuring the space between two stacked labels with the caliper reads the same number as the stack's Gap
Nothing about how text renders changes: no line is clipped and no wrap moves
